description: Curated sauce ingredients, pairings, and classification for the Sauce Lab.

sauces.name: Béchamel
sauces.instructions: Melt butter, whisk in flour to form a roux and cook 2 minutes without browning. Gradually add warm milk while whisking constantly until smooth and thickened. Season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.

sauces.name: Mornay
sauces.instructions: Prepare a béchamel base, then stir in grated gruyère and parmesan off heat until melted and smooth. Season with nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.

sauces.name: Soubise
sauces.instructions: Sweat sliced onions in butter until very soft but not browned. Stir in flour, cook briefly, then add milk and simmer until thick. Purée until smooth and finish with cream.

sauces.name: Alfredo
sauces.instructions: Melt butter with cream over medium heat until simmering. Remove from heat and stir in grated parmesan until emulsified and silky. Season with salt, pepper, and a hint of nutmeg.

sauces.name: Cheddar Sauce
sauces.instructions: Make a roux with butter and flour, then whisk in milk until thickened. Remove from heat and stir in shredded cheddar and mustard until smooth. Season with cayenne and salt.

sauces.name: Velouté
sauces.instructions: Make a blond roux with butter and flour, cooking until lightly golden. Gradually whisk in warm chicken stock and simmer for 20 minutes, skimming as needed. Strain and season.

sauces.name: Suprême
sauces.instructions: Prepare a chicken velouté, then reduce by one-third. Finish with heavy cream and a squeeze of lemon juice, then mount with cold butter for richness.

sauces.name: Allemande
sauces.instructions: Make a velouté with veal stock, then temper egg yolks with cream and whisk into the sauce off heat. Add lemon juice and nutmeg, stirring until thickened without boiling.

sauces.name: Bercy
sauces.instructions: Sweat shallots in butter, add white wine and reduce by half. Add fish stock thickened with a light roux and simmer. Finish with butter, parsley, and lemon juice.

sauces.name: Espagnole
sauces.instructions: Cook a dark brown roux, add mirepoix and tomato paste, then deglaze with veal stock. Simmer 2-3 hours with thyme and bay leaf, skimming often. Strain through fine mesh.

sauces.name: Demi-glace
sauces.instructions: Combine equal parts Espagnole and rich veal stock, then reduce by half until the sauce coats a spoon. Skim frequently during reduction for clarity. Finish with meat glaze for depth.

sauces.name: Bordelaise
sauces.instructions: Reduce red wine with shallots, thyme, and bay leaf by two-thirds. Add demi-glace or enriched veal stock and simmer until nappé. Mount with cold butter and season.

sauces.name: Chasseur
sauces.instructions: Sauté shallots in butter, deglaze with white wine and reduce. Add diced tomatoes and demi-glace, simmer until thickened. Finish with fresh tarragon and parsley.

sauces.name: Robert
sauces.instructions: Sweat onions in butter until soft, deglaze with white wine and vinegar, reduce by half. Add demi-glace and simmer. Finish with Dijon mustard off heat—do not boil after adding mustard.

sauces.name: Madeira Sauce
sauces.instructions: Reduce Madeira wine with shallots by half, add demi-glace and meat glaze, then simmer until glossy. Mount with cold butter and strain. The wine's sweetness should balance the savory stock.

sauces.name: Tomato Sauce (Classic French)
sauces.instructions: Sweat mirepoix and garlic in olive oil, add tomato purée and paste with herbs. Simmer 45 minutes until rich and concentrated. Strain for a smooth classic French tomato sauce.

sauces.name: Marinara
sauces.instructions: Gently sauté garlic in olive oil until fragrant, add crushed tomatoes and simmer 20-30 minutes. Stir in basil and oregano near the end. Keep it simple—quality tomatoes are key.

sauces.name: Arrabbiata
sauces.instructions: Sauté garlic and dried chilies in olive oil until fragrant and lightly golden. Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 20 minutes. The sauce should be noticeably spicy. Finish with parsley.

sauces.name: Puttanesca
sauces.instructions: Dissolve anchovies in olive oil with garlic, add tomatoes, olives, and capers. Simmer 20 minutes until rich and briny. Season with chili flake and oregano—go easy on salt as ingredients are salty.

sauces.name: Bolognese
sauces.instructions: Brown meat and pancetta, add soffritto and cook until soft. Add wine and reduce, then tomato paste, purée, and milk. Simmer low and slow for 2-3 hours. The milk tenderizes and adds sweetness.

sauces.name: Hollandaise
sauces.instructions: Whisk egg yolks with water over a double boiler until thick and pale. Slowly drizzle in warm clarified butter while whisking constantly. Finish with lemon juice, salt, and cayenne.

sauces.name: Béarnaise
sauces.instructions: Reduce vinegar with shallots, peppercorns, and half the tarragon until nearly dry. Strain, whisk with yolks over gentle heat, then emulsify with clarified butter. Finish with fresh tarragon.

sauces.name: Choron
sauces.instructions: Prepare a béarnaise base, then fold in concentrated tomato paste for color and sweetness. The tomato should complement, not overpower, the tarragon and butter flavors.

sauces.name: Mousseline
sauces.instructions: Prepare a standard hollandaise, then fold in softly whipped cream just before serving. The cream lightens the texture and mellows the richness. Serve immediately.

sauces.name: Teriyaki
sauces.instructions: Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar; bring to a simmer. Add ginger and garlic, cook until sugar dissolves. Thicken with cornstarch slurry and simmer until glossy.

sauces.name: Ponzu
sauces.instructions: Combine soy sauce, yuzu juice, rice vinegar, mirin, and dashi. Steep bonito flakes in the mixture overnight, then strain. The citrus should brighten the umami base.

sauces.name: Kung Pao
sauces.instructions: Toast dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns in oil until fragrant. Add garlic and ginger, then the sauce mixture of soy, vinegar, wine, sugar, and cornstarch. Toss with peanuts and finish with sesame oil.

sauces.name: Sweet and Sour Sauce
sauces.instructions: Combine vinegar, sugar, ketchup, and soy sauce; bring to a simmer. Add garlic and ginger. Thicken with cornstarch slurry until the sauce is glossy and coats a spoon.

sauces.name: Black Bean Sauce
sauces.instructions: Stir-fry garlic and ginger, add fermented black bean paste and shaoxing wine. Add soy sauce, sugar, and a splash of water; thicken with cornstarch. Finish with sesame oil and scallions.

sauces.name: XO Sauce
sauces.instructions: Rehydrate and mince dried shrimp. Slowly fry garlic, shallots, chilies, and shrimp in oil until deeply caramelized and crispy. Season with soy sauce and sugar. Store in oil.

sauces.name: Thai Green Curry
sauces.instructions: Fry green curry paste in coconut cream until fragrant and oil separates. Add remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, and palm sugar. Simmer, then finish with Thai basil and kaffir lime leaves.

sauces.name: Thai Red Curry
sauces.instructions: Crack coconut milk and fry red curry paste until oil separates and paste is fragrant. Add remaining coconut milk, season with fish sauce and palm sugar. Finish with lime juice and Thai basil.

sauces.name: Pad Thai Sauce
sauces.instructions: Dissolve palm sugar in warm tamarind pulp, then stir in fish sauce and rice vinegar. The balance should be equally sweet, sour, and salty. Add crushed peanuts and lime juice at serving.

sauces.name: Peanut Sauce (Thai)
sauces.instructions: Simmer red curry paste in coconut milk, add ground peanuts and stir until smooth. Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind. Adjust with lime juice for brightness.

sauces.name: Yangnyeom
sauces.instructions: Combine gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, and sugar; heat until sugar dissolves. Add garlic and ginger, simmer briefly. Finish with sesame oil and rice vinegar for a sticky, spicy-sweet glaze.

sauces.name: Bulgogi Marinade
sauces.instructions: Whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, garlic, ginger, and pepper. Add scallions and sesame seeds. Use as a marinade for thinly sliced beef, letting it rest at least 30 minutes for flavor absorption.

sauces.name: Gochujang Sauce
sauces.instructions: Whisk gochujang with sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, and soy sauce until smooth. Add minced garlic and sesame seeds. Serve as a dipping sauce or bibimbap topping—no cooking required.

sauces.name: Tonkatsu Sauce
sauces.instructions: Whisk together ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and mustard until smooth. Simmer briefly to meld flavors. The sauce should be thick, tangy, and slightly sweet.

sauces.name: Tare
sauces.instructions: Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and dashi; bring to a gentle simmer. Cook until sugar dissolves and sauce reduces slightly. Use as a concentrated seasoning base for ramen or yakitori.

sauces.name: Tikka Masala
sauces.instructions: Fry onion, garlic, and ginger in ghee, add dry spices and bloom until fragrant. Add tomato purée and simmer 15 minutes. Finish with cream for a rich, mildly spiced sauce.

sauces.name: Makhani (Butter Chicken)
sauces.instructions: Cook onion, garlic, and ginger in ghee; add spices and tomato purée, simmer until thick. Blend smooth, return to heat, stir in cream, butter, and fenugreek. The sauce should be velvety and mildly sweet.

sauces.name: Korma
sauces.instructions: Toast whole spices in ghee, add onion, garlic, and ginger. Stir in ground almonds and yogurt, simmer gently without boiling to prevent curdling. Finish with cream for a mild, aromatic sauce.

sauces.name: Vindaloo
sauces.instructions: Fry mustard seeds, then add onion, garlic, ginger, and ground spices. Add vinegar and tomato purée; simmer until thick and intensely spiced. The vinegar tang is essential to authentic vindaloo.

sauces.name: Saag
sauces.instructions: Blanch and purée spinach. Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in ghee with spices. Add puréed greens and simmer to meld flavors. Finish with cream. Use a mix of spinach and mustard greens for depth.

sauces.name: Raita
sauces.instructions: Squeeze excess water from grated cucumber and fold into yogurt. Add toasted cumin, mint, salt, and a pinch of cayenne. Chill before serving as a cooling accompaniment to spicy dishes.

sauces.name: Mango Chutney
sauces.instructions: Cook diced mango with sugar, vinegar, ginger, and spices until thick and jammy, about 20 minutes. The chutney should balance sweet, sour, and spicy. Cool before serving.

sauces.name: Mint Chutney
sauces.instructions: Blend mint, cilantro, lime juice, ginger, cumin, and salt with a splash of water until smooth. Adjust consistency as needed. Serve fresh—the bright green color fades over time.

sauces.name: Mole Poblano
sauces.instructions: Toast and rehydrate dried chilies. Blend with charred aromatics, chocolate, nuts, seeds, and spices until smooth. Fry the paste in lard, then thin with stock and simmer 30 minutes for complexity.

sauces.name: Mole Negro
sauces.instructions: Char chilies until blackened for signature dark color. Blend with chocolate, fried plantain, charred aromatics, and spices. Fry the paste in lard, thin with stock, and simmer 45 minutes. The darkest of all moles.

sauces.name: Salsa Roja
sauces.instructions: Roast tomatoes, jalapeños, onion, and garlic under a broiler until charred. Blend to desired texture—chunky or smooth. Season with lime juice, cilantro, cumin, and salt.

sauces.name: Salsa Verde
sauces.instructions: Boil or roast tomatillos and jalapeños until soft. Blend with onion, garlic, cilantro, and lime juice. The sauce should be bright, tangy, and green. Adjust heat with jalapeño seeds.

sauces.name: Chimichurri
sauces.instructions: Finely chop parsley and combine with oregano, garlic, vinegar, olive oil, and chili flakes. Let rest 30 minutes for flavors to meld. Do not blend—the texture should be rustic and chunky.

sauces.name: Sofrito
sauces.instructions: Slowly cook onion and garlic in olive oil until deeply soft and golden. Add tomatoes, cumin, and oregano, cook until jammy. This aromatic base forms the foundation of countless Latin dishes.

sauces.name: Adobo Sauce
sauces.instructions: Toast and rehydrate dried chilies. Blend with garlic, onion, cumin, oregano, and vinegar until smooth. The sauce should be thick, earthy, and moderately spicy with smoky chipotle notes.

sauces.name: Ají Amarillo Sauce
sauces.instructions: Blend ají amarillo peppers with garlic, onion, lime juice, and olive oil until smooth. The sauce has a distinctive fruity heat and vibrant yellow color. Finish with fresh cilantro.

sauces.name: Tahini Sauce
sauces.instructions: Whisk tahini with lemon juice—it will seize and thicken first, then loosen as you add water gradually. Add garlic, salt, and cumin. Adjust consistency with more water as needed.

sauces.name: Toum
sauces.instructions: Purée garlic with salt, then very slowly drizzle in oil and lemon juice alternately while blending to form a thick, fluffy emulsion. The process is similar to making mayonnaise—patience is essential.

sauces.name: Zhug
sauces.instructions: Blend cilantro, jalapeños, garlic, and spices with olive oil until a rough paste forms. Add lemon juice and salt. The Yemeni hot sauce should be fiery, herbal, and intensely aromatic.

sauces.name: Harissa
sauces.instructions: Rehydrate dried chilies, then blend with garlic, toasted spices, olive oil, and lemon juice into a thick paste. The North African chili paste should be smoky, earthy, and moderately hot.

sauces.name: Romesco
sauces.instructions: Blend roasted peppers, tomato, toasted almonds, and garlic with olive oil until slightly chunky. Season with smoked paprika, vinegar, and cayenne. The Catalan sauce should be thick and nutty.

sauces.name: Chermoula
sauces.instructions: Blend cilantro, parsley, garlic, and spices with olive oil and lemon juice into a thick marinade. The North African herb sauce works as both a marinade and finishing sauce. Rest 30 minutes before using.

sauces.name: Groundnut Sauce
sauces.instructions: Fry onion, garlic, and ginger in palm oil. Add ground peanuts, tomato paste, and stock; simmer until thick and creamy. Add scotch bonnet whole for gentle heat. The sauce should coat a spoon.

sauces.name: Shito
sauces.instructions: Blend dried shrimp, crayfish, scotch bonnets, and aromatics into a paste. Fry slowly in palm oil with tomato paste for 30-40 minutes until dark and oil separates. The Ghanaian hot pepper sauce keeps well in oil.

sauces.name: Peri Peri
sauces.instructions: Blend scotch bonnets, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, and spices with olive oil until smooth. The Portuguese-African sauce should be fiery and bright. Use as a marinade or table sauce.

sauces.name: Berbere Sauce
sauces.instructions: Cook onion in ghee until deeply browned, add garlic and ginger. Toast berbere spice until fragrant, add tomato paste and water. Simmer until thick. This Ethiopian spiced base is used for doro wat and other stews.

sauces.name: BBQ Sauce
sauces.instructions: Combine all ingredients and simmer 20-30 minutes until thick and glossy. The sauce should balance sweet, smoky, tangy, and mildly spicy flavors. Adjust sugar and vinegar to taste.

sauces.name: Buffalo Sauce
sauces.instructions: Melt butter and whisk with cayenne hot sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire, and garlic. The classic ratio is equal parts butter to hot sauce. Serve immediately—the emulsion breaks as it cools.

sauces.name: Gravy (Southern)
sauces.instructions: Make a roux with butter and flour (or pan drippings), cook until lightly golden. Whisk in milk gradually and simmer until thick. Season generously with black pepper—this is a pepper-forward gravy.

sauces.name: Remoulade
sauces.instructions: Fold mustard, capers, cornichons, parsley, and seasonings into mayonnaise. Add lemon juice and cayenne for brightness and heat. Chill at least 1 hour for flavors to meld.

sauces.name: Aji Sauce
sauces.instructions: Deseed aji amarillo peppers and blend with garlic and lime juice until smooth. Fold into mayonnaise and season with salt. Chill before serving.

sauces.name: Nuoc Cham
sauces.instructions: Dissolve sugar in warm water. Add fish sauce and lime juice. Mince garlic and thinly slice thai chili, stir in. Let sit 10 minutes for flavors to meld.

sauces.name: Beurre Blanc
sauces.instructions: Mince shallot and simmer with white wine until reduced to 2 tablespoons. Over low heat, whisk in cold butter one tablespoon at a time until emulsified. Finish with lemon juice and salt.

sauces.name: Beurre Noisette
sauces.instructions: Melt butter over medium heat and cook, swirling occasionally, until milk solids turn golden brown and it smells nutty. Remove from heat immediately, add lemon juice, capers, and chopped parsley.

sauces.name: Gastrique
sauces.instructions: Cook sugar in a dry saucepan over medium heat until it caramelizes to a deep amber. Carefully add vinegar (it will sputter) and stir until dissolved. Add fruit puree and simmer until slightly thickened.

sauces.name: Chimichurri Verde
sauces.instructions: Finely chop parsley, oregano, and garlic. Combine in a bowl with olive oil, red wine vinegar, and red pepper flakes. Let rest at least 30 minutes before serving.

sauces.name: Dashi
sauces.instructions: Soak kombu in water for 30 minutes. Heat slowly until just before boiling, then remove kombu. Bring to a boil, add bonito flakes, and immediately remove from heat. Let steep 5 minutes, then strain.

sauces.name: Salsa Macha
sauces.instructions: Heat oil and fry dried chilies, peanuts, garlic, and sesame seeds until toasted and fragrant. Let cool slightly, then blend or chop to desired consistency. Store submerged in the frying oil.
